sources.title: Niger Humanitarian Situation Report No. 3 (End-of-Year), 31 December 2025
sources.temporal_coverage: Humanitarian conditions and UNICEF-supported responses during 1 January–31 December 2025; report dated 8 February 2026.

claims.locator: Printed pp. 1–2 (PDF pp. 1–2), humanitarian needs overview.
claims.paraphrase: Report links 2025 violence and climate shocks to 459,585 displaced people; 60% were children.

claims.locator: Printed p. 2 (PDF p. 2), 2025 SMART/SENS and Harmonized Framework findings.
claims.paraphrase: 2025 global acute malnutrition was 17.1% in Diffa; parts of Maradi and Zinder were critical.

claims.locator: Printed p. 2 (PDF p. 2), flooding and education-infrastructure impacts.
claims.paraphrase: Floods affected 77,506 households, destroying 60,388 homes; 316 classrooms sheltered families, disrupting 26,235 students.

claims.locator: Printed p. 4 (PDF p. 4), Essential Household Items and local contingency planning.
claims.paraphrase: Seven Diffa communes updated contingency plans; 50 monitors trained, two simulations held and seven sites prepared.

claims.locator: Printed p. 4 (PDF p. 4), Social protection, drought cash programme results.
claims.paraphrase: After the 2022 drought, cash paid 26,977 households in 17 municipalities across five regions four CFAF 45,000 cycles.
institutions: National Mechanism for the Prevention and Management of Food Crises
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: UNICEF reports improved consumption and coping.

claims.locator: Printed p. 4 (PDF p. 4), beneficiary registration in five municipalities.
claims.paraphrase: Registration covered 77,028/80,000 target households in five municipalities; insecurity in northern Bagaroua constrained access.

access_audit.locator: Opened all 10 PDF pages; claims use printed pp. 1–2 and 4 (PDF pp. 1–2 and 4).
access_audit.notes: Original UNICEF PDF body inspected. Cover gives 8 February 2026 and reporting period 1 January–31 December 2025; 2025 conditions are not treated as current 2026.
access_audit.reuse_terms: Terms not reviewed; concise paraphrases only.

access_audit.locator: Direct PDF opened but returned only a URL line, not report text.
access_audit.notes: Indexed result text was excluded; no claim relies on it.

search_audit.query: Niger 2025 floods Tillaberi Diffa Tahoua Maradi local districts UNICEF humanitarian situation report official
search_audit.outcome: Opened UNICEF's original 2025 end-year report; retained dated district nutrition and vulnerability findings.

search_audit.query: Niger 2025 2026 report climate shocks conflict displacement Tillaberi Diffa livelihoods humanitarian response UN FAO
search_audit.outcome: The opened UNICEF report explicitly describes violence and climate shocks alongside displacement and protection/service risks.

search_audit.query: Niger conflict displacement climate vulnerability displaced host communities flood drought impacts reverse link 2025 UNHCR official
search_audit.outcome: The opened report documents access constraints from insecurity in northern Bagaroua affecting drought-response beneficiary registration; a UNHCR regional report could not be opened and was excluded.

search_audit.query: Niger local resilience capacity climate flood drought WASH anticipatory action villages 2025 FAO UNICEF official
search_audit.outcome: The opened report describes local contingency plans, simulation exercises, shock-responsive cash support and anticipatory action; outputs are not independent impact evaluations.

gaps: The report's 2025 displacement total combines violence and climate shocks without separating their respective contributions; it does not establish climate-caused armed violence.
The 2026 UNICEF mid-year report PDF returned only a URL line when opened; its indexed text was excluded.
UNHCR's 2024 flood-impact report could not be directly opened because the publisher returned HTTP 429; search text was excluded.
UNICEF outputs are historical operational reports; self-reported capacity and cash-transfer effects were not independently evaluated.
